title: A whole conclusion preserves promise’s scope

captions.physics: Completing discussion with agreement’s scope clear
captions.energy: Preserving the value of accepted words
captions.emotions: Feeling proportion between participation and expectation

meaning: You can complete discussion with agreement’s scope clear and preserve an accepted value of words given, feeling proportion between participation and expectation without dismissing an unnamed request.
text: On your Vishuddha, the World in the physical position appears in completing discussion with agreement’s scope clear. The Hierophant in energy supports a value of words given accepted by both. Justice in emotions brings proportion between participation and expectation. You can gather promises and wishes into an understandable conclusion without mixing them. A shared norm helps respect actual agreement rather than assign blame through disappointment’s intensity.

For example, you finish an argument about a missed call: agreement concerned a brief reply, while a long conversation was only wanted as a proposal. **A whole conclusion distinguishes a promise from a wish still alive**. Accepted words and what was missing can both be recognised. A sense of measure emerges: wanting was heard without becoming an earlier debt. Yet respect for agreement does not declare a long exchange unnecessary. It can be requested now without retrospectively rewriting acceptance already given.

Difficulty arises if an accepted norm recognises only previously promised things as important. Accuracy becomes a way not to hear a new request. The constructive Hierophant helps preserve words’ significance alongside respectful living approach. You can reject an unnamed obligation and seriously discuss a wish; proportion requires neither removing disappointment nor guaranteeing future readiness, while clearly finishing an earlier question leaves room for another answer without repeating the old argument.
